extracted.intended_audience: GAP users and developers (people writing GAP code, packages, and methods)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for using GAP operations (process calls, object/mutability APIs, types/families/filters) and for implementing new objects/methods that obey GAP's semantics (mutability, copying, types, filters, families).

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenExternal(filename)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open the file filename using the default application for this file in the operating system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to open files like HTML and PDF files in the GUI. (Function signature: OpenExternal(filename)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process(dir, prg, stream-in, stream-out, options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process runs a new process and returns when the process terminates. It returns the return value of the process if the operating system supports such a concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements and recommendations: dir must be a directory object (affects current directory for relative paths); use DirectoryTemporary() if the process creates temporary or log files because GAP will try to remove those directories on quitting; for package-related programs prefer DirectoriesPackageLibrary or DirectoriesPackagePrograms only if necessary (to avoid accumulating logs in package dir). prg should be a filename (prefer the result of Filename(...)) and pass IsExecutableFile; Process does no searching through directories (use PathSystemProgram or Filename to locate binaries). stream-in should be one of: InputTextNone, InputTextUser, an unopened InputTextFile, or InputTextString; Process may consume all input even if program does not require it. stream-out should be one of: OutputTextNone, OutputTextUser, an unopened OutputTextFile, or OutputTextString. options is a list of strings passed directly as command-line arguments (no shell substitutions, each string passed as one arg even if it contains spaces); input/output redirection commands are not allowed as options. Use PathSystemProgram to find system programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exec(cmd, option1, ..., optionN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exec runs a shell in the current directory to execute the command given by the string cmd with options option1 , ..., optionN .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: cmd is interpreted by the shell so shell features (redirection, quoting, etc.) may be used. Exec calls the more general operation Process. Example: Exec("echo \"GAP is great!\" > foo"); Exec("cat foo"); Exec("rm foo"); Use Edit(...) to call an editor from within GAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PathSystemProgram / Filename to find system programs
rubrics_metrics.description: To find a system program use PathSystemProgram (9.5.2). prg should be the result of Filename(…) and should pass IsExecutableFile (9.7.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process itself does no searching through a list of directories; Filename performs searching. Example: date := PathSystemProgram("date"); returns "/bin/date".

rubrics_metrics.name: IsObject(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsObject returns true if the object obj is an object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It obviously can never return false. It can be used as a filter in InstallMethod when one of the arguments can be anything.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements as equivalence classes
rubrics_metrics.description: The equality operation "=" defines an equivalence relation on all GAP objects. The equivalence classes are called elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three reasons to regard different objects as equal: same information stored in different places; same info stored in different ways (e.g., sparse vs dense); different information equal modulo a mathematical equivalence (e.g., a and a^3 when a^2=1). The manual uses this distinction to explain behavior of objects, representations, and domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sets (in GAP manual usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the manual, 'set' often means a domain or a strictly sorted list (IsSSortedList); two domains are equal iff they have the same elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A domain and a list can be compared with "=": true iff the list equals the strictly sorted list of elements of the domain. See discussion of sorted lists and sets (21.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Domains are objects whose underlying abstraction is a structured set (e.g., a group, conjugacy class, vector space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equality of domains is always equality as sets (contain the same elements). Domains are central in GAP; many objects exist primarily to form domains and compute properties of them. See Chapter 31 for domain descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical objects vs equal objects; IsIdenticalObj(obj1,obj2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two objects are identical if they actually refer to the same area of computer memory; identical objects describe the same element. IsIdenticalObj tests whether obj1 and obj2 are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: two copies of a simple constant may or may not be stored as identical internally. For mutable objects it's important to know identity vs equality. Examples in the manual show consequences: two equal but non-identical lists change independently; if identical, changes affect both. Use IsIdenticalObj to detect identity. If objects are identical then IsIdenticalObj returns true; otherwise false.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsNotIdenticalObj(obj1,obj2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether the objects obj1 and obj2 are not identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple complementary operation to IsIdenticalObj.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutability (definition and implementer responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: An object is immutable if its mathematical value (as defined by =) does not change under any operation; mutable objects may be changed to represent different mathematical objects during their life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers must ensure that functions and methods they write never change immutable objects mathematically. Many objects are immutable (e.g., permutations). Mutable objects include lists, records, etc. Use Immutable or MakeImmutable to obtain immutable versions when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsCopyable(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mutable form of an object obj can be made in GAP, the object is called copyable. IsCopyable tests for this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lists and records are copyable. A new mutable version can be obtained via ShallowCopy. Objects that only have immutable form are constants (e.g., integers, permutations, domains); calling Immutable or ShallowCopy on a constant returns the argument itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsMutable(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether obj is mutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an object is mutable then it is also copyable and a ShallowCopy method should be supplied for it. Important: IsMutable must not be implied by another filter (else Immutable could create paradoxical objects where IsMutable is false but the implying filter is true). Use IsMutable to detect whether mutable operations are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immutable(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Immutable returns an immutable structural copy of obj in which the subobjects are immutable copies of the subobjects of obj. If obj is immutable then Immutable returns obj itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP will complain with an error if one tries to change an immutable object. Use Immutable to safely store shared immutable structures (e.g., identity matrices, lists of generators).

rubrics_metrics.name: MakeImmutable(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Turns the (mutable or immutable) object obj into an immutable one; this also makes all subobjects of obj immutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use MakeImmutable if obj and its mutable subobjects are newly created — otherwise use Immutable. It is not possible to turn an immutable object into a mutable one; only mutable copies can be made. Immutable objects may store knowledge (e.g., whether a list is strictly sorted) as long as the mathematical value remains the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutability of Iterators
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterators are mutable (and thus copyable). Every call of NextIterator changes a mutable iterator until it is exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ShallowCopy(iter) returns a mutable iterator that has no mutable data in common with iter, and that behaves equally w.r.t. IsDoneIterator and NextIterator. Immutable(iter) will yield an immutable (but not very useful) iterator; behavior of shallow copy for iterators must be explicitly defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutability rules for results of arithmetic operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many operations return immutable results (attributes like Size, Zero, One, Inverse). Arithmetic operations such as +, -, *, /, ^, mod, unary -, Comm, LeftQuotient return mutable results except if all arguments are immutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: product of two matrices is immutable iff both matrices are immutable. There are exceptions where result is less deeply nested than arguments. For convenience, 0 * obj is ZeroSameMutability(obj), -obj is AdditiveInverseSameMutability(obj), obj^0 is OneSameMutability(obj), obj^-1 is InverseSameMutability(obj). Operations ZeroOp, AdditiveInverseOp, OneOp, InverseOp return mutable results whenever a mutable version exists, contrary to the attributes. Methods installed for arithmetic operations must obey the rule about the mutability of the result; this allows avoiding expensive copies when operands are immutable. For low-level in-place algorithms use dedicated mutable constructors/operations (e.g., TransposedMatMutable, TriangulizeMat).

rubrics_metrics.name: ShallowCopy(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: ShallowCopy returns a new mutable object equal to its argument, if this is possible. The subobjects of ShallowCopy(obj) are identical to the subobjects of obj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If GAP does not support a mutable form of the immutable object obj then ShallowCopy returns obj itself. For copyable objects the definition reflects 'first level copying'. See specific ShallowCopy definitions for lists/matrices (21.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: StructuralCopy(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: StructuralCopy returns a copy scp such that scp and obj are identical if obj is immutable; otherwise scp is a mutable copy of obj where each subobject of scp is a structural copy of the corresponding subobject of obj, and identical subobjects of obj correspond to identical subobjects of scp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both ShallowCopy and StructuralCopy return obj itself if obj is not copyable. Example in manual shows how identical subobjects are handled and how immutable subobjects remain identical in the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetName(obj, name) and Name(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: SetName sets a name (a string) for an object for viewing; Name returns that previously assigned name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name is used only for viewing the object via this name. There are no methods installed for computing names automatically, but the name may be set for suitable objects. Example: R := PolynomialRing(Integers,2); SetName(R,"Z[x,y]"); printing R shows Z[x,y]; Name(R) returns "Z[x,y]".

rubrics_metrics.name: InfoText(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: InfoText(obj) is an attribute: a mutable string with information about the object obj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no default method to create an info text; it's an attribute that can be defined for suitable objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInternallyConsistent(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: For debugging purposes, IsInternallyConsistent checks the consistency of an object obj composed from other (composed) objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a default method with rank zero that returns true. It is possible and recommended to check consistency of subobjects recursively via IsInternallyConsistent. Note that IsInternallyConsistent is not an attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: MemoryUsage(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the amount of memory in bytes used by the object obj and its subobjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determining memory usage is recursive and may itself use memory. The procedure descends into lists and records, positional and component objects; it deliberately does not take into account type and family objects. For functions, it only counts the body, not the local context (though the function keeps a reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of objects (family + filters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every GAP object has a type consisting of two main parts: the family and a collection of filters (bit-list). The type determines whether an operation is admissible and how it is performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filters include categories, representations, attribute testers and properties. Partial types are intersections of parts. Detailed understanding of the type system is not required to use GAP but helps to understand behavior and method selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Families (semantics & creation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Families form a partition of all GAP objects such that equal objects (w.r.t. =) lie in the same family, and the family of the result of an operation depends only on the families of its operands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Families are used in method selection (relations like ReturnTrue, IsIdenticalObj, IsCollsElms). Families may be created dynamically when needed (e.g., elements of a finitely presented group). Choosing families when creating new objects: make them large enough to form interesting domains but small enough to allow useful relations. Collections and domains have special family behavior (a collection's family is the collections family of the element family). Be cautious about enlarging existing families because of installed implications/filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: FamilyObj(obj) and NewFamily(name[, req[, imp[, famfilter]]])
rubrics_metrics.description: FamilyObj(obj) returns the family of obj. NewFamily creates a new family with optional req (a required filter), imp (a filter in which fam will lie), and famfilter (a filter that will hold for the family object itself). Families are represented as component objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If req is present, fam is subset of req and creating an object in fam not in req triggers an error. If imp is present, any object created in fam will lie in imp automatically. Components can store information about the family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filters (definition and semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: A filter is a unary GAP function that returns true or false indicating membership in the set defined by the filter; filters are implemented as positions in the bitlist part of a type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filters express different aspects of object information (categories, representations, attribute testers, properties). The intersection (meet) of filters is again a filter (e.g., IsList and IsEmpty). A simple filter is one not expressible as a meet; each simple filter corresponds to a bitlist position. Every filter has a rank (used for method ranking).

rubrics_metrics.name: RankFilter(filt), NamesFilter(filt), FilterByName(name), ShowImpliedFilters(filter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations for inspecting filters: RankFilter returns the rank of a filter; NamesFilter returns a list of names of implied simple filters; FilterByName finds a filter by its name; ShowImpliedFilters displays filters implied by a given filter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank for simple filters is assigned incrementally on creation; for composite filters it's the sum of incremental ranks. NamesFilter lists implied simple filters. ShowImpliedFilters prints unconditional implications and those requiring further filters (indicated with '+'). Example: ShowImpliedFilters(IsNilpotentGroup) prints many implied filters and may show 'May imply with: +IsFinitelyGeneratedGroup'.

rubrics_metrics.name: FiltersType(type) and FiltersObj(object)
rubrics_metrics.description: FiltersType(type) and FiltersObj(object) return the list of filters in a type or in the type of object respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for inspecting the filters that constitute the type information for objects and types.
